titleEn: The Glory of Kings — Azariah Praises the Queen and Her Land, and Recites the Laws and Curses (ch. 90)
part: ch. 90 — Azariah Praises the Queen and Her Land, and Recites the Laws and Curses
about: Azariah, one of the Israelites who came with Menelik, answers the queen’s call by praising her wisdom and her country. He says that his people long held themselves chosen, but that Ethiopia is better than Judah, and that the dark faces of its people are its one blemish, though if God lights up their hearts none will find them strange (?). He then bids them keep from what God hates and recites the laws he promises to teach: honesty about a neighbour’s goods and strayed animals, justice for the poor, orphan and stranger, care for birds and gleanings, and the curses of Deuteronomy 27, with a warning against images and idols. He cites Psalm 125:3 (the rod of sinners on the lot of the righteous), gives a saying on teaching others the good, and closes with a precept against usury.

sentences.t: ፺ ፡ ኀበ ፡ ወደሳ ፡ አዛርያስ ፡ ለንግሥት ፡ ወለሀገራ ።
sentences.l: 90. Where praised-her Azariah to-queen and-to-country-her.
sentences.i: Chapter 90: How Azariah praised the queen and her country.
sentences.n: Chapter heading, a unit of its own, built like the headings of chs. 88 and 89: ኀበ opens a title-like clause, ‘how’ rather than ‘where’ (?). ወደሳ is ወደሰ ‘praise’ (3ms perfect; its ወ is a root letter, not ‘and’) + -ኣ ‘her’, the queen; the object is then repeated by ለንግሥት, the doubling Geʿez likes (as in ch. 89’s heading). ወለሀገራ ‘and her country’ is ወ- + ለ- (marking the object again, as in ለንግሥት) + ሀገር ‘country’ + the 3fs suffix, written -ራ.

sentences.t: ወተንሥአ ፡ አዛርያስ ፡ ወይቤላ ፡ ለንግሥት ፡ ኦእግዝእትነ ፡ በአማን ፡ አልቦ ፡ ዘይትማሰለኪ ፡ በጥበብ ፡ ወበአእምሮ ፡ ወተውህበ ፡ ለኪ ፡ እምኀበ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ ዘእንበለ ፡ እግዚእየ ፡ ንጉሥ ፡ ዘአብጽሐነ ፡ ውስተ ፡ ዛቲ ፡ ምድር ፡ ምስለ ፡ እግዝእትነ ፡ ጽዮን ፡ ቅድስት ፡ ሰማያዊት ፡ ታቦተ ፡ ሕጉ ፡ ለእግዚኣብሔር ።
sentences.l: And-arose Azariah and-said-to-her to-queen: O-our-lady, in-truth not-is who-resembles-you in-wisdom and-in-knowledge, and-was-given to-you from-with God, except my-lord king who-brought-us into this land with our-lady Zion, holy, heavenly, ark-of law-his of-God.
sentences.i: And Azariah arose and said to the queen, ‘O our lady, truly there is no one like you in wisdom and knowledge, and it was given to you from God, except my lord the king, who brought us into this land together with our lady Zion, the holy and heavenly one, the ark of God’s law.
sentences.n: ወተንሥአ ‘and he arose’ (ወ- + ተንሥአ, 3ms perfect) and ወይቤላ ‘and he said to her’ (ይቤ + ላ); the addressee is then repeated, ለንግሥት, the doubling Geʿez likes. ኦእግዝእትነ is ኦ (vocative) + እግዝእት ‘lady’ + -ነ ‘our’. አልቦ ‘there is not’ is the standard ‘no one/nothing’; ዘይትማሰለኪ is ዘ- ‘who’ + the ተማ- stem of መሰለ (ተማሰለ, ‘be like, be compared with’; 3ms imperfect) + -ኪ ‘you (f)’; አእምሮ is ‘knowledge’, kept apart from ልቡና ‘understanding’ as in ch. 89. ተውህበ is the passive of ወሀበ ‘give’. ዘእንበለ ‘except, apart from’ (recurs often), here qualifying the whole claim: no one equals you except the king. ዘአብጽሐነ is ዘ- + causative አብጽሐ ‘bring’ (from በጽሐ ‘arrive’) + -ነ ‘us’. The last chain is apposition: ጽዮን, then ቅድስት ‘holy’, ሰማያዊት ‘heavenly’, then ታቦተ ሕጉ ‘ark of his law’ (construct state, -ተ ending, as ታቦተ ኪዳኑ later). Azariah’s speech opens here and runs to the end of the part.

sentences.t: ንሕነሰ ፡ ወአበዊነ ፡ ቀደምት ፡ ንቤ ፡ አልቦ ፡ ዘኀረየ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ ዘእንበለ ፡ ቤተ ፡ ያዕቆብ ፡ ኪያነ ፡ ኀረየ ፡ ወኪያነ ፡ አብዝኀ ፡ ወኪያነ ፡ ሠምረ ፡ ወአንገሠነ ፡ ወረሰየነ ፡ ሰብአ ፡ ቤቱ ፡ ወመማክርቲሁ ፡ ለስብሐቲሁ ፡ ወለታቦተ ፡ ኪዳኑ ፡ ወሀገርኒ ፡ ንብል ፡ አልቦ ፡ ዘኀረየ ፡ ዘእንበለ ፡ ሀገርነ ፤
sentences.l: As-for-us and-fathers-our ancients we-said: not-is who-chose God except house-of Jacob; us he-chose and-us he-multiplied and-us he-favoured and-made-us-king and-made-us people-of house-his and-counsellors-his for-glory-his and-for-ark-of covenant-his; and-country-too we-say: not-is who-chose except country-our;
sentences.i: As for us and our fathers of old, we used to say that God chose no one except the house of Jacob. Us he chose, us he multiplied, us he favoured; he made us kings and made us the people of his house and his counsellors, for his glory and for the ark of his covenant. And of the country, too, we say that he chose none other than our country;
sentences.n: ንሕነሰ ‘as for us’: ንሕነ ‘we’ + the contrastive -ሰ (this -ሰ recurs: ወይእዜሰ, ለእመሰ). ንቤ is the 1cp of ይቤ ‘say’, ‘we said/used to say’ (I read it as a habitual past). ዘኀረየ is ዘ- + ኀረየ ‘choose’. The object pronoun ኪያነ ‘us’ is fronted three times (ኪያነ ኀረየ… ወኪያነ አብዝኀ… ወኪያነ ሠምረ) for emphasis: ‘us he chose’. አንገሠነ is the causative of ነግሠ ‘reign’, so ‘made us kings’; ወረሰየነ is ረሰየ ‘make, set’ + -ነ. ቤተ ያዕቆብ, ሰብአ ቤቱ ‘people of his house’ (ch. 88’s rendering), ታቦተ ኪዳኑ are construct chains; መማክርቲሁ is ‘his counsellors’ (plural + -ሁ). ወሀገርኒ: ሀገር + the additive -ኒ ‘also’. The claim of election for ‘the house of Jacob’ is the Israelite party’s own; the next unit turns it to Ethiopia.

sentences.t: ወይእዜሰ ፡ ርኢነ ፡ እንተ ፡ ትኄይስ ፡ ሀገረ ፡ ኢትዮጵያ ፡ እምብሔረ ፡ ይሁዳ ፤
sentences.l: And-now-indeed we-saw which is-better country-of Ethiopia than-land-of Judah;
sentences.i: but now we have seen that the country of Ethiopia is better than the land of Judah;
sentences.n: ወይእዜሰ ‘and now, indeed’ (ይእዜ ‘now’ + -ሰ). ርኢነ is ርእየ ‘see’, 1cp perfect. እንተ ትኄይስ ‘which is better’: እንተ is the feminine relative (agreeing with ሀገረ), ትኄይስ the 3fs imperfect of ኀየሰ ‘be good, be better’, with እም- ‘than’ for the comparison: እምብሔረ ይሁዳ ‘than the land of Judah’. ሀገረ ኢትዮጵያ is the accusative/construct, in apposition to the unexpressed object of ‘we saw’.

sentences.t: ወእምከመ ፡ በጻሕነ ፡ ውስተ ፡ ብሔርክሙ ፡ ሠነየነ ፡ ኵሉ ፡ ዘርኢነ ፡ ማይክሙኒ ፡ ሠናይ ፡ ወትሁቡ ፡ ዘእንበለ ፡ ሤጥ ፡ ወነፋስ ፡ ዘእንበለ ፡ መረዋሕት ፡ ወጸቃውዕ ፡ ከመ ፡ ጽንጒነ ፡ መርሕብ ፡ ወእንስሳ ፡ ከመ ፡ ኆጻ ፡ ባሕር ፡ ወእምዘ ፡ ርኢነ ፡ አልቦ ፡ ሕሱመ ፡ ወአልቦ ፡ ፀዋገ ፡ እምዘ ፡ ንሰምዕ ፡ ወእምዘ ፡ ንከይድ ፡ ወእምዘ ፡ ን ፡ ገስስ ፡ ወእምዘ ፡ ንጥዕም ፡ በአፉነ ፤
sentences.l: And-when we-arrived into land-your, pleased-us all what we-saw; water-your-also good and-you-give without price; and-air without መረዋሕት and-ጸቃውዕ like ጽንጒነ-of plain and-livestock like sand-of sea; and-than-what we-saw not-is defective(?) and-not-is affliction(?), than-what we-hear and-than-what we-tread(?) and-than-what we-touch and-than-what we-taste with-mouth-our;
sentences.i: And when we reached your land, everything we saw pleased us. Your water, too, is good, and you give it without price; and the air is without መረዋሕት (?) and ጸቃውዕ (?), like the ጽንጒነ (?) of the open plain, and the livestock are like the sand of the sea. Of all we saw there was nothing defective (?) and no affliction (?), in what we heard, in what we trod on (?), in what we touched, and in what we tasted with our mouths;
sentences.n: A catalogue of the land’s praise. ወእምከመ ‘and when’; በጻሕነ is በጽሐ ‘arrive’ (1cp perfect); ሠነየነ is ሠነየ ‘be good, please’ + -ነ ‘us’. ማይክሙኒ is ማይ ‘water’ + -ክሙ ‘your’ + -ኒ ‘too’. ትሁቡ I take as 2mp imperfect of ወሀበ (‘you give’); ዘእንበለ ሤጥ ‘without price’. CRUX: መረዋሕት, ጸቃውዕ and ጽንጒነ are words I cannot fix without Dillmann (the sentence seems to praise air and abundance, ‘like the … of the open plain’; መርሕብ is ‘broad place’), so they are left untranslated and marked (?). ሕሱመ ‘defective’ and ፀዋገ ‘affliction’ are also uncertain (?): parts 49–50 and 81 give ፀዋግ as ‘captor (?)’ and ‘grim (?)’, so ‘affliction’ here is only a guess from its pairing with ሕሱመ; ሕሱመ may be the same word as ሕሡመ in the curse on the deaf below (ሰ/ሠ). ንከይድ is ከይደ ‘tread, go’ (?), the senses then being hearing, treading, touch, taste (sight is ርኢነ); I do not find a verb of smelling in the form. The word printed ን ፡ ገስስ (with a stray ፡ inside; kept as printed) is ንገስስ, 1cp imperfect of ገሰሰ ‘touch, feel’. The repeated እምዘ ‘of what’ (እም- + ዘ) ties the four senses together.

sentences.t: ወባሕቱ ፡ እምእንተ ፡ ትኔጽር ፡ አሐቲ ፡ ሀለወት ፡ ኮንክሙ ፡ ጸሊማነ ፡ በገጽ ፡ ወዘንተ ፡ ዘእቤ ፡ በዘ ፡ ርኢኩ ፡ ወባሕቱ ፡ ለእመ ፡ አብርሀ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ አልባቢክሙ ፡ አልቦ ፡ ዘይነኪየክሙ ።
sentences.l: But than-which looks one is-there: you-became black in-face; and-this what I-say by-what I-saw; but if illumined God hearts-your not-is who-finds-you-strange(?).
sentences.i: But among all that meets the eye one thing remains: that you are dark of face. What I say, I say from what I have seen. But if God lights up your hearts, there will be no one who finds you strange, or does you harm (?).
sentences.n: A delicate turn, said with care. እምእንተ ትኔጽር አሐቲ ሀለወት ‘from (among) what one looks at, one (thing) there is’ (ትኔጽር 3fs/impersonal imperfect of ነጸረ ‘look’; I read it as ‘of all that is seen’). ኮንክሙ is ኮነ in the 2mp perfect (-ክሙ ‘you’, as the glossary has it), ‘you are, have become’; ጸሊማነ ‘dark’ is the plural predicate; በገጽ ‘in face’ (በ- ‘in’). ዘእቤ is ዘ- + 1cs imperfect ‘I say’; በዘ ርኢኩ ‘by what I saw’. ለእመ ‘if’ (recurs, also ለእመሰ); አብርሀ is the causative of በርሀ ‘shine’ (‘illumine’), cf. Ephesians 1:18 (hearts enlightened) (?). ዘይነኪየክሙ is ዘ- + a 3ms imperfect + -ክሙ ‘you’; its last radical is -y, not the -r of ነኪር ‘strange, foreign’, so the link with ነኪር is doubtful: ‘finds you strange’ is a guess, and a different root, perhaps ‘harm’, is possible (?).

sentences.t: ወባሕቱ ፡ ተገሐሡ ፡ እማውታ ፡ ወደም ፡ ወብትክ ፡ ወዝሙት ፡ ወእምኵሉ ፡ ዘይጸልእ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ ከመ ፡ ንትፈሣሕ ፡ ብክሙ ፡ ሶበ ፡ ንሬኢየክሙ ፡ እንዘ ፡ ትፈርሁ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ ወእንዘ ፡ ትርዕዲ ፡ እምቃሉ ፤
sentences.l: But turn-aside from-the-dead(?) and-blood and-ብትክ and-fornication and-from-all what hates God, so-that we-rejoice in-you when we-see-you while you-fear God and-while you-tremble from-word-his;
sentences.i: But turn aside from the dead (?), from blood, from cutting (?), and from fornication, and from everything that God hates, so that we may rejoice in you when we see you fearing God and trembling at his word;
sentences.n: ተገሐሡ is the imperative (2mp) of ተገሐሠ ‘turn aside’ (the house rendering of chs. 88–89; with እም- ‘from’, ‘turn aside from’, i.e. keep away from); the prohibitive of the same verb, ኢትትገሐሡ, comes in the next sentence but one, and ተገሐሥ/ይትገሐሡ again later. እማውታ I read as እም- ‘from’ + ማውታ ‘the dead’ (the same word is in እጓለ ማውታ ‘orphan’, below: ‘child of the dead’). Beside ‘blood’ and ‘fornication’ the list may recall Acts 15:20 (?), which would make እማውታ ‘what has died of itself’ (?). ብትክ I take as ‘cutting’ (from በተከ ‘cut off’), perhaps the gashing forbidden in Leviticus 19:28 (?). ዘይጸልእ ‘what hates’: ዘ- + ጸልአ. ከመ ንትፈሣሕ ‘so that we rejoice’: ከመ + the 1cp subjunctive. ሶበ ‘when’ (also ‘if’); እንዘ + imperfect gives ‘while’ (እንዘ ትፈርሁ ‘while you fear’). ትርዕዲ has the ending -ዲ (2fs), but the sense is plural, ‘you tremble’ (ርዕደ): a slip for ትርዕዱ or a collapsed ending (?).

sentences.t: በከመ ፡ አዘዞሙ ፡ እግዚአብሔር ፡ ለአበዊነ ፡ ወይቤሎ ፡ ለሙሴ ፡ አዝዞሙ ፡ በኵሉ ፡ ወንግሮሙ ፡ ከመ ፡ ይዕቀቡ ፡ ሕግየ ፡ ወሥርዐትየ ፤
sentences.l: As-commanded-them God to-fathers-our and-said-to-Moses: command-them in-all and-tell-them that they-keep law-my and-ordinance-my;
sentences.i: as God commanded our fathers, and said to Moses, “Command them in everything, and tell them to keep my law and my ordinance;”
sentences.n: በከመ ‘as, according as’ (with a perfect, the standing way of citing scripture; recurs below in ‘as our prophets foretold’ and ‘as David said’). አዘዞሙ is አዘዘ ‘command’ + -ሙ ‘them’; ወይቤሎ ለሙሴ ‘and he said to Moses’ (ሎ is singular, ‘to him’); አዝዞሙ, ወንግሮሙ are imperatives with -ሙ. ከመ ይዕቀቡ ‘that they keep’ is ከመ + 3mp subjunctive. ሕግየ ‘my law’, ሥርዐትየ ‘my ordinance’ (-የ ‘my’). The Divine command to ‘keep my statutes’ echoes Deuteronomy 4:1-2, 5:31 and 6:1; no one verse is quoted. Printed እግዚአብሔር here, without the ኣ of the usual spelling.

sentences.t: ወኢትትገሐሡ ፡ ኢለየማን ፡ ወኢለፀጋም ፡ እምዘ ፡ ንኤዝዘክሙ ፡ ዮም ፡ ወይእዜኒ ፡ ከመ ፡ ታምልክዎ ፡ ለእግዚኣብሔር ፡ ቅዱሰ ፡ እስራኤል ፡ ወትግበሩ ፡ ሥምረቶ ፡ እስመ ፡ መነኖሙ ፡ ለሕዝብነ ፡ በከመ ፡ ተነበዩ ፡ ነቢያቲነ ፡ ወኀረየ ፡ ኪያክሙ ፤
sentences.l: And-not turn-aside neither-to-right nor-to-left from-what we-command-you today; and-now, that you-serve to-God holy-one-of Israel and-do will-his, for rejected-them to-people-our as prophesied prophets-our and-chose you;
sentences.i: and do not turn aside, to the right or to the left, from what we command you today. And now serve God, the Holy One of Israel, and do his will; for he has rejected our people, as our prophets foretold, and has chosen you.
sentences.n: ወኢትትገሐሡ ‘and do not turn aside’: ኢ- + 2mp imperfect; ኢለየማን ወኢለፀጋም ‘neither to the right nor to the left’ (ኢ + ለ-, the pairs recur), the phrase of Deuteronomy 5:32 and 28:14. ንኤዝዘክሙ ‘we command you’ (a form of አዘዘ, 1cp + -ክሙ); ዮም ‘today’. ወይእዜኒ ‘and now’. ከመ ታምልክዎ ‘that you serve him’ (አምለከ ‘worship, serve’); ቅዱሰ እስራኤል ‘Holy One of Israel’ is the title of Isaiah. ሥምረቶ ‘his good pleasure, will’ (from ሠምረ, as in ወኪያነ ሠምረ above). CRUX of sense: መነኖሙ ለሕዝብነ is መነነ ‘reject, spurn’ + -ሙ + ለ- ‘our people’, the Israelite speaker saying that God has rejected his own people (Judah), as ‘our prophets’ (ነቢያቲነ) foretold; I take ኪያክሙ ‘you’ as the Ethiopians, fronted as ኪያነ was before. The sentence ends at ፤.

sentences.t: አኮኑ ፡ ለኵልክሙ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ ፈጣሪክሙ ፡ ምንተ ፡ ይሰአኖ ፡ ለእግዚኣብሔር ፡ ለእመ ፡ አፍቀረ ፡ ኪያነ ፡ ወጸልአ ፡ ኪያሆሙ ፡ እስመ ፡ ኵሉ ፡ ሎቱ ፡ ወኵሉ ፡ ተግባሩ ፡ ወአልቦ ፡ ዘይሰአኖ ፡ ለእግዚኣብሔር ፡ አምላከ ፡ እስራኤል ።
sentences.l: Is-it-not to-all-of-you God creator-your? What is-hard-for-him to-God if he-loved us and-hated them? for all to-him and-all work-his; and-not-is what is-hard-for-him to-God, God-of Israel.
sentences.i: Is not God the creator of all of you? What is too hard for God, if he loved us and hated them? For everything is his and everything is his handiwork; and nothing is too hard for God, the God of Israel.
sentences.n: አኮኑ is አኮ ‘not’ + the question particle -ኑ, ‘is it not (so)’. ፈጣሪክሙ ‘your creator’ (ፈጣሪ + -ክሙ); ኵልክሙ ‘all of you’ (ኵል + -ክሙ). ይሰአኖ is ሰአነ ‘be unable, be hard’ + -ኖ ‘to him’: ‘what is too hard for him’ (?), the rhetorical question of Genesis 18:14; I render it ‘what is too hard for’, as in the last clause of the unit. ለእመ አፍቀረ ኪያነ ወጸልአ ኪያሆሙ ‘if he loved us and hated them’ echoes Malachi 1:2-3 (‘Jacob I loved, Esau I hated’). ተግባር is ‘work, creature’; ሎቱ ‘to him, his’. The doubled ‘to God’ (ለእግዚኣብሔር) is the usual Geʿez restatement of the subject.

sentences.t: ወስምዑ ፡ እንግርክሙ ፡ ትእዛዞ ፤
sentences.l: And-hear: I-tell-you commandments-his;
sentences.i: And listen: I will tell you his commandments;
sentences.n: ወስምዑ ‘and hear’ (imperative of ሰምዐ); እንግርክሙ is the 1cs subjunctive ‘that I tell you’, ‘let me tell you’, of ነገረ + -ክሙ. ትእዛዞ is ትእዛዝ ‘commandment’ + -ሁ, contracted to -ዞ. What follows is a run of precepts from Exodus 23, Leviticus 19, Deuteronomy 22-27, in the order of the author’s mind rather than of any book; only the first is numbered.

sentences.t: ፩ ፡ ኢይትኀየል ፡ ካልኦ ፡ ወኢትሂዲ ፡ ንዋየ ፡ ቢጽክሙ ፡ ወኢትትሓመዩ ፡ ወኢትትዓመፁ ፡ ወኢትትላኰዩ ፤
sentences.l: 1. not be-strong-against another and-not carry-off(?) goods-of neighbour-your and-not harm-one-another(?) and-not wrong-one-another and-not ተላኰዩ;
sentences.i: 1. Let no one use force against another; do not carry off (?) your neighbour’s goods; do not injure one another (?), do not wrong one another, and do not ተላኰዩ (?) with one another;
sentences.n: The numeral ፩ is a word on its own (the build gives it role ‘num’). ኢይትኀየል ‘let him not prevail against’ (ተኀየለ ‘be strong’), ካልኦ ‘another’. ኢትሂዲ is a singular-looking prohibitive of a verb I cannot place with confidence (ሄደ ‘go’? ‘take away’?) (?). The three plural prohibitions ኢትትሓመዩ, ኢትትዓመፁ, ኢትትላኰዩ are in the reciprocal ተ- stem (‘to one another’): ተዓመፀ is from ዐመፀ ‘do wrong’; ተሓመየ and ተላኰየ I cannot fix (?): ‘injure’ for ኢትትሓመዩ is only a guess, and ተላኰዩ is left untranslated. ንዋየ ቢጽክሙ: ንዋይ ‘goods’ in the construct state, ቢጽ ‘neighbour, fellow’ + -ክሙ. This pattern of ኢ- + 2mp imperfect (the plural ending -u on the last consonant: -ዩ, -ኡ, -ጹ and so on) is the prohibition throughout the list.

sentences.t: ወለእመቦ ፡ ዘአተወ ፡ እንስሳ ፡ ምስለ ፡ ንዋይክሙ ፡ እምንዋየ ፡ ቢጽክሙ ፡ ኢትትዐወርዎ ፡ አላ ፡ አግብኡ ፡ ሎቱ ፡ ወለእመሰ ፡ ኢያእመርክሙ ፡ ባዕለ ፡ ንዋዩ ፡ አጽንዑ ፡ ሎቱ ፡ ወእምከመ ፡ ረከበ ፡ አግብኡ ፡ ሎቱ ፡ ንዋዮ ፤
sentences.l: And-if-there-is who led-in(?) animal with goods-your from-goods-of neighbour-your, not turn-a-blind-eye-to-him, but return to-him; and-if you-not-know owner-of goods-his, keep for-him; and-when he-found, return to-him goods-his;
sentences.i: And if someone has driven (?) an animal in among your goods, one from your neighbour’s goods, do not turn a blind eye to it, but give it back to him; and if you do not know the owner of the goods, keep it for him; and when he comes upon it (?), give him back his goods;
sentences.n: The law of the strayed animal: Exodus 23:4, Deuteronomy 22:1-3. ወለእመቦ ‘and if there is’ (ለእመ ‘if’ + ቦ ‘there is’), then ዘአተወ ‘one who led/drove in’ (አተወ, which I take as ‘drive an animal’) (?). ኢትትዐወርዎ ‘do not turn a blind eye to it’ (ተዐወረ ‘pretend blindness’, cf. Deuteronomy 22:1 ‘do not hide yourself’); አግብኡ ‘give back’ (imperative of አግብአ), አጽንዑ ‘hold fast, keep’. ባዕለ ንዋዩ ‘owner of his goods’ (ባዕል ‘lord, owner’ in the construct). ወእምከመ ረከበ ‘and when he found’: whether the owner finds it or the finder finds the owner is not fixed by the form (?). ሎቱ ‘to him’ doubled by ንዋዮ ‘his goods’.

sentences.t: ወእመቦ ፡ ዘወድቀ ፡ ንዋየ ፡ ቢጽክሙ ፡ ውስተ ፡ ግብ ፡ አው ፡ ውስተ ፡ ዐዘቅት ፡ አው ፡ ውስተ ፡ ቀላይ ፡ አው ፡ ውስተ ፡ ጸድፍ ፡ ኢትትዐደዉ ፡ ወኢትትኀለፉ ፡ እስከ ፡ ትነግርዎ ፡ ወታስተላዕልዎ ፤
sentences.l: And-if-there-is what fell goods-of neighbour-your into pit or into well or into mire or into ጸድፍ, not pass-by and-not go-past until you-tell-him and-lift-it;
sentences.i: And if your neighbour’s goods have fallen into a pit, or a well, or a mire, or a ጸድፍ (?), do not pass by or go on until you have told him and lifted it up;
sentences.n: Deuteronomy 22:4 (a fallen ox or ass; cf. Exodus 23:5). ዘወድቀ is ዘ- + ወድቀ ‘fall’, ‘(something) that fell’. The four places are joined by አው ‘or’, each with ውስተ ‘into’: ግብ ‘pit’, ዐዘቅት ‘well, pit’, ቀላይ ‘mire’ (?), ጸድፍ which I cannot fix (?). ኢትትዐደዉ ‘do not pass over’ (ተዐደወ), ኢትትኀለፉ ‘do not go by’; እስከ ትነግርዎ ‘until you tell him’; ታስተላዕልዎ is the causative አስተላዕለ ‘raise up’ (2mp imperfect + -ዎ ‘it’).

sentences.t: ወእመኒቦ ፡ ዘከረየ ፡ ዐዘቅተ ፡ ወዘሐነጸ ፡ ማኅፈደ ፡ ኢይኅድግ ፡ ዘእንበለ ፡ መክደን ፡ ወተድባብ ፤
sentences.l: And-if-anyone-there-is who-dug well and-who-built tower, not let-leave without cover and-parapet;
sentences.i: And if there is anyone who has dug a well or built a tower (?), let him not leave it without a cover and a parapet (?);
sentences.n: Exodus 21:33-34 (the uncovered pit) and Deuteronomy 22:8 (the parapet on a new house). ወእመኒቦ ‘and if there is anyone’ (ወ + እመ + -ኒ + ቦ). ዘከረየ ‘who dug’ (ዐዘቅተ ‘a well’, as above), ዘሐነጸ ‘who built’ (ሐነጸ ‘build’); ማኅፈድ ‘tower, high building’ (?). ኢይኅድግ ‘let him not leave’; መክደን ‘cover’ (the instrumental መ- noun from ከደነ ‘cover’), ተድባብ ‘roof, parapet, canopy’ (?).

sentences.t: ወለእመኒቦ ፡ ዘጾረ ፡ ጾረ ፡ ክቡደ ፡ አው ፡ ለእመኒ ፡ ቦዘጸዓነ ፡ ዘወድቆ ፡ ኢትኅልፉ ፡ ዘእንበለ ፡ ታስተላዕልዎ ፡ ወታቅልሉ ፡ ሎቱ ፡ እስመ ፡ እኁክሙ ፡ ውእቱ ፤
sentences.l: And-if-anyone-there-is who-bore burden heavy or if there-is who-loaded(?) one-that fell-to-him(?), not pass-by without you-lift-him and-lighten for-him, for brother-your he;
sentences.i: And if someone is carrying a heavy load, or if someone has loaded up and it has fallen on him (?), do not pass by without lifting it up and lightening it for him, for he is your brother;
sentences.n: Deuteronomy 22:4 and Exodus 23:5 again. ዘጾረ ጾረ ክቡደ ‘who bore a heavy burden’ (ጾረ ‘carry’; the verb with its own noun, ጾር, as object, then ክቡድ ‘heavy’). አው ለእመኒ ‘or if’; ቦዘጸዓነ is printed as one word and read as ቦ ዘጸዓነ ‘there is one who loaded’ (ጸዓነ ‘load’), kept as printed. ዘወድቆ ‘(that) fell to him’ (?). The Geʿez names no animal; the ass and ox of the Pentateuch laws are not read in. ኢትኅልፉ ‘do not pass’ + ዘእንበለ ‘without’ + the subjunctive ታስተላዕልዎ ‘that you lift it’; ታቅልሉ is አቅለለ ‘lighten’. እኁክሙ ‘your brother’ (እኁ ‘brother’ + -ክሙ).

sentences.t: ወኢታብስሉ ፡ እጐልተ ፡ በሐሊበ ፡ እሙ ፤
sentences.l: And-not cook kid in-milk-of mother-its;
sentences.i: And do not boil a kid in its mother’s milk;
sentences.n: Exodus 23:19, 34:26; Deuteronomy 14:21. ኢታብስሉ is the causative አብሰለ ‘cook, boil’ (2mp prohibitive); እጐልተ ‘young animal, kid’ (accusative); በሐሊበ እሙ ‘in the milk of its mother’ (ሐሊብ ‘milk’ in the construct state before እሙ, from እም + -ሁ).

sentences.t: ወኢትግምጹ ፡ ፍትሐ ፡ ምስኪን ፡ ወእጓለ ፡ ማውታ ፤
sentences.l: And-not pervert judgment-of poor-man and-child-of dead (orphan);
sentences.i: And do not pervert the judgment of the poor man or of the orphan;
sentences.n: Exodus 23:6; Deuteronomy 24:17. ኢትግምጹ is ገምጸ ‘pervert, twist’; ፍትሐ ምስኪን ‘the judgment of the poor’ (construct). እጓለ ማውታ is ‘child of the dead’, the usual word for ‘orphan’: እጓል ‘child’ + ማውታ ‘the dead’ (cf. ተገሐሡ above).

sentences.t: ወኢታድልዉ ፡ ለገጽ ፡ ወኢትንሥኡ ፡ ሕልያነ ፡ ለገሚጸ ፡ ፍትሕ ፡ ወለስምዐ ፡ ሐሰት ፤
sentences.l: And-not show-partiality to-face and-not take bribes(?) for-perverting judgment and-for-witness-of falsehood;
sentences.i: And do not show partiality to a person’s face, and do not take bribes (?) to pervert judgment or to give false witness;
sentences.n: Exodus 23:8; Deuteronomy 16:19. ኢታድልዉ ለገጽ ‘do not show partiality to a face’ (አድለወ ‘incline, be partial’; the noun in በአድልዎ, below). ሕልያነ is the plural of ሕልይ ‘gift’, here ‘bribes’ (?). ለገሚጸ ፍትሕ ‘for the perverting of judgment’ and ለስምዐ ሐሰት ‘for witness of falsehood’ are purpose phrases with ለ-, the second a construct chain (ሐሰት ‘falsehood’).

sentences.t: ወሶበ ፡ ትረክቡ ፡ ዖፈ ፡ በውስተ ፡ ምድርክሙ ፡ ምስለ ፡ አፍኅርቲሃ ፡ ታሕይዉ ፡ ኪያሃ ፡ ወኢትንሥኡ ፡ ደቂቃ ፡ ከመ ፡ ይኑኅ ፡ መዋዕሊክሙ ፡ በዲበ ፡ ምድር ፡ ወይትባረኩ ፡ ዘርእ ፡ ክሙ ፡ ለነዋኅ ፡ መዋዕል ፤
sentences.l: And-when you-find bird in land-your with fledglings(?)-her, spare her and-not take young-her, that be-long days-your upon earth and-be-blessed seed-your for-length-of days;
sentences.i: And when you find a bird in your land with her fledglings (?), let her live, and do not take her young, so that your days may be long on the earth and your seed may be blessed for length of days;
sentences.n: After Deuteronomy 22:6-7, where the mother is let go and the young may be taken; as written here both are spared (ታሕይዉ ኪያሃ, the causative አሕየወ ‘let live’, then ኢትንሥኡ ደቂቃ ‘do not take her young’). ሶበ ትረክቡ ‘when you find’; ዖፍ ‘bird’; አፍኅርቲሃ ‘her fledglings’ (?). ከመ ይኑኅ መዋዕሊክሙ ‘that your days be long’ (ኖኅ ‘be long’) is the promise of Deuteronomy 22:7. The word printed ዘርእ ፡ ክሙ (a stray ፡ inside) is ዘርእክሙ ‘your seed’, kept as printed; ይትባረኩ is a plural verb with ‘seed’ as collective. ለነዋኅ መዋዕል ‘for length of days’.

sentences.t: ወሶበ ፡ ተዐጽዲ ፡ ማእረረ ፡ እክልክሙ ፡ ኢትጠናቀቁ ፡ ዐጺደ ፡ ወዘወድቀሂ ፡ ኢትእርዩ ፡ ወዘረሳዕክሙ ፡ ክልስስተ ፡ ኅድጉ ፡ ተመዪጠክሙ ፡ ኢትንሥኡ ፡ አላ ፡ ኅድጉ ፡ ለግዩረ ፡ ሀገርክሙ ፡ ከመ ፡ ይባርክ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ ፍሬ ፡ ምድርክሙ ፤
sentences.l: And-when you-reap harvest-of grain-your not be-exacting(?) reaping, and-what fell-too not gather(?), and-what you-forgot sheaf(?) leave; turning-back-your not take, but leave for-stranger-of country-your that bless God fruit-of land-your;
sentences.i: And when you reap the harvest of your grain, do not be too exacting (?) in the reaping, and do not gather (?) what has fallen; leave the sheaf (?) you have forgotten, and do not turn back to take it, but leave it for the stranger in your country, so that God may bless the fruit of your land;
sentences.n: Leviticus 19:9-10, 23:22; Deuteronomy 24:19-21 (the gleanings for the stranger, orphan and widow). ተዐጽዲ has the 2fs ending -ዲ but a plural sense (cf. ትርዕዲ above): ‘you reap’ (ዐጸደ). ዐጺደ is the verbal noun ‘reaping’ in the accusative, ‘as to reaping’. ማእረረ እክልክሙ ‘the harvest of your grain’ (construct). ኢትጠናቀቁ is a ተ-stem form of ጠነቀቀ ‘be careful, exact’; the stem label and the meaning are my reading (?). ኢትእርዩ ‘do not pick up/gather’ (?); ዘረሳዕክሙ ‘what you forgot’ (ረሰዐ), ክልስስት ‘sheaf’ (?); ተመዪጠክሙ ‘your turning back’ (the verbal noun of ተመይጠ). ለግዩረ ሀገርክሙ ‘for the stranger of your country’; ግዩር ‘stranger, alien’ returns in a later curse.

sentences.t: ወኢትግበሩ ፡ ርኩሰ ፡ ወኢትፍትሑ ፡ በአድልዎ ፡ ወኢትግበሩ ፡ ዐመፃ ፡ በኵሉ ፡ ዘትትናገሩ ፡ ከመ ፡ ትትባረኩ ፡ ወከመ ፡ ይብዛኅ ፡ ፍሬ ፡ ምድርክሙ ፡ ወከመ ፡ ትድኀኑ ፡ እመርገመ ፡ ሕግ ፡ ዘአዘዘ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ ከመ ፡ ይርግምዎ ፡ ለገባሬ ፡ እኪት ፡ ወጸሐፈ ፡ እንዘ ፡ ይብል ፡ ዘያስሕቶ ፡ ፍኖቶ ፡ ለዕዉር ፡ ርጉም ፡ ውእቱ ፤
sentences.l: And-not do uncleanness, and-not judge with-partiality, and-not do injustice in-all what you-talk-about, so-that you-be-blessed and-so-that increase fruit-of land-your and-so-that you-be-saved from-curse-of law which commanded God that they-curse the-doer-of evil, and-wrote saying: who leads-him-astray way-his to-blind cursed he;
sentences.i: And do not do anything unclean, and do not judge with partiality, and do not do injustice in anything you speak of, so that you may be blessed, and the fruit of your land may increase, and you may be saved from the curse of the law which God commanded, that they should curse the doer of evil. And he wrote, saying: Whoever leads the blind astray from his way is cursed;
sentences.n: The long unit (32 words) that leads into the curses is kept whole because its only ፤ is at its end. ርኩስ ‘uncleanness’, በአድልዎ ‘with partiality’, ዐመፃ ‘injustice, wrong’. Three purpose clauses with ከመ + subjunctive (ትትባረኩ, ይብዛኅ, ትድኀኑ). እመርገመ ሕግ ‘from the curse of the law’ (እም + መርገም, construct). ከመ ይርግምዎ ‘that they curse (him)’, an indefinite plural, with ለገባሬ እኪት ‘the doer of evil’; ወጸሐፈ ‘and he wrote’ (the subject is not named: God, the last subject, or Moses (?)). The curses are those of Deuteronomy 27:15-26, each with the formula ርጉም ውእቱ ‘cursed is he’ (ርጉም ‘cursed’ + the pronoun ውእቱ), which repeats below with ዘ- + verb as the subject. This first one is Deuteronomy 27:18 (the blind): ዘያስሕቶ is ዘ- + the causative of ስሕተ ‘err’ + -ሁ ‘him’ (the blind man, named again by ለዕዉር); ፍኖቶ ‘his way’, ዕዉር ‘blind’.

sentences.t: ወዘይነግሮ ፡ ሕሡመ ፡ ለጽሙም ፡ ርጉም ፡ ውእቱ ፤
sentences.l: And-who tells-him ill(?) to-deaf(?) cursed he;
sentences.i: And whoever speaks ill (?) to the deaf (?) is cursed;
sentences.n: The formula ርጉም ውእቱ (see the previous unit). ዘይነግሮ ሕሡመ ለጽሙም: ዘ- + ነገረ + -ሁ, then ሕሡም ‘ill, defect’ (?), perhaps the same word as ሕሱመ in the praise of the land above (ሠ/ሰ) and ጽሙም ‘deaf, dumb’ (?). I cannot match this to a verse of Deuteronomy 27 (the nearest is Leviticus 19:14, ‘do not curse the deaf’), so the sense is a hedged reading.

sentences.t: ወዘአርኰሰ ፡ ምስካበ ፡ አቡሁ ፡ ርጉም ፡ ውእቱ ፤
sentences.l: And-who defiled bed-of father-his cursed he;
sentences.i: And whoever has defiled his father’s bed is cursed;
sentences.n: Deuteronomy 27:20. ዘአርኰሰ ‘who defiled’ (the causative አርኰሰ of ረኰሰ ‘be unclean’; ዘ- here takes a perfect). ምስካበ አቡሁ ‘the bed of his father’ (construct: ምስካብ, with አቡሁ ‘his father’).

sentences.t: ወዘይዘብጥ ፡ ቢጾ ፡ በጒሕሉት ፡ ርጉም ፡ ውእቱ ፤
sentences.l: And-who strikes neighbour-his in-secret cursed he;
sentences.i: And whoever strikes his neighbour in secret is cursed;
sentences.n: Deuteronomy 27:24. ዘይዘብጥ ‘who strikes’ (ዘበጠ; the passive ተዘብጠ comes below); ቢጾ ‘his neighbour’ (ቢጽ + -ሁ); በጒሕሉት ‘in secret, by stealth’ (?), a word that recurs below.

sentences.t: ወዘይገምጽ ፡ ፍትሐ ፡ ግዩር ፡ ከመ ፡ ይቅትል ፡ ደመ ፡ ንጹሕ ፡ ርጉም ፡ ውእቱ ፤
sentences.l: And-who perverts judgment-of stranger so-that he-kills blood-of innocent cursed he;
sentences.i: And whoever perverts the stranger’s judgment so as to kill the innocent is cursed;
sentences.n: A blend of Deuteronomy 27:19 (the stranger’s right) and 27:25 (the bribe to slay the innocent). ዘይገምጽ ‘who perverts’ (as ኢትግምጹ above); ከመ ይቅትል ‘so that he kills’; ደመ ንጹሕ ‘innocent blood’ (construct + adjective), here the thing killed, i.e. the blameless person.

sentences.t: ዘያስተአኪ ፡ አቡሁ ፡ ወእሞ ፡ ርጉም ፡ ውእቱ ፤
sentences.l: Who dishonours father-his and-mother-his cursed he;
sentences.i: Whoever dishonours his father and his mother is cursed;
sentences.n: Deuteronomy 27:16. ዘያስተአኪ is a causative-reflexive (አስተአከየ) ‘treat as base, dishonour’ (?), with its object አቡሁ ወእሞ ‘his father and his mother’ (እም + -ሁ, contracted). Like the curse on the killer below, it begins without ወ-.

sentences.t: ወኵሉ ፡ ዘይገብር ፡ ግልፎ ፡ ወስብኮ ፡ ዘርኩስ ፡ ግብረ ፡ እደ ፡ ሰብእ ፡ ወይሠይሞ ፡ ወየኀብኦ ፡ ውስተ ፡ ቤቱ ፡ ወይሰግድ ፡ ሎቱ ፡ ከመ ፡ አምላክ ፡ ኢአሚኖ ፡ ከመ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ ፈጣሬ ፡ ሰማያት ፡ ወምድር ፡ ዘገብሮ ፡ ለአዳም ፡ በዘ ፡ ዚአሁ ፡ አርአያ ፡ ወአምሳል ፡ ወሤሞ ፡ ላዕለ ፡ ኵሉ ፡ ዘፈጠረ ፡ ወኵልነ ፡ ተግባሩ ፡ ንሕነ ፡ ዘንተ ፡ ዘኢየአምን ፡ ርጉመ ፡ ለይኩን ፡ አሜን ፤
sentences.l: And-all who makes carving-his and-casting-his which unclean work-of hands-of man and-sets-it and-hides-it in house-his and-bows to-him as god, not-believing that God maker-of heavens and-earth who-made-him to-Adam in-what his-own image and-likeness and-set-him over all that he-created and-all-of-us creatures-his we, this who not-believes cursed let-be, Amen;
sentences.i: And everyone who makes a carved image or a cast image, an unclean work of human hands, and sets it up and hides it in his house and bows down to it as a god, not believing that God is the maker of heaven and earth, who made Adam in his own image and likeness and set him over all he created, and that we are all his creatures: whoever does not believe this, let him be cursed. Amen;
sentences.n: Deuteronomy 27:15 (the carved or cast image, ‘an abomination, the work of the hands of a craftsman’), widened with the creed of Genesis 1:26-28 and Psalm 8:6. ግልፎ ‘his carving’ (ግልፍ + -ሁ) and ስብኮ ‘his casting’ (ስብክ), the -ሁ standing for a possessive that English leaves out; ዘርኩስ ‘which is unclean’. ይሠይሞ is ሠየመ ‘set up, appoint’ + -ሁ; የኀብኦ ‘hides it’ (ኀብአ); ይሰግድ ሎቱ ‘bows down to him/it’. ኢአሚኖ is a negated participle ‘not believing’, with ከመ ‘that’. ዘገብሮ ለአዳም ‘who made Adam’ (ገብሮ = ገብረ + -ሁ) በዘ ዚአሁ አርአያ ወአምሳል ‘in his own image and likeness’ (ዘ ዚአሁ ‘of his own’), the Genesis 1:26 pair, noted in the pilot chapter too. ወሤሞ ‘and set him’ (ሠየመ + -ሁ). ተግባር ‘work, handiwork’. Then the oath of the curse: ዘንተ ዘኢየአምን ‘this one who does not believe’, ርጉመ ለይኩን ‘let him be cursed’ (ለይኩን the jussive ‘let him be’); አሜን is Amen, the people’s response in Deuteronomy 27:15. At 40 words it is under the cut limit and kept whole.

sentences.t: ወዘይሰክብ ፡ ምስለ ፡ እንስሳ ፡ ርጉመ ፡ ለይኩን ፤
sentences.l: And-who lies with animal cursed let-be;
sentences.i: And whoever lies with an animal, let him be cursed;
sentences.n: Deuteronomy 27:21. ዘይሰክብ ‘who lies’ (ሰከበ ‘lie down’). The previous curse already closed with ርጉመ ለይኩን ‘let him be cursed’ (predicate in the accusative); from here on the curses take this form instead of ርጉም ውእቱ ‘he is cursed’.

sentences.t: ወዘይሰክብ ፡ ምስለ ፡ ተባዕት ፡ ከመ ፡ ዘምስለ ፡ አንስት ፡ ርጉመ ፡ ለይኩን ፤
sentences.l: And-who lies with male as who-with women cursed let-be;
sentences.i: And whoever lies with a male as with women, let him be cursed;
sentences.n: Leviticus 18:22 and 20:13. ተባዕት ‘male’ and አንስት ‘women’ (the plural of ብእሲት ‘woman’); ከመ ዘምስለ አንስት ‘as (he who lies) with women’.

sentences.t: ዘይቀትል ፡ ነፍሰ ፡ ደመ ፡ ንጹሐ ፡ በዐመፃ ፡ ወበጒሕሉት ፡ ርጉመ ፡ ለይኩን ፡ ወእምኵሉሰ ፡ ኢታምልኩ ፡ ባዕደ ፡ አማልክተ ፡ እስመ ፡ ቀናኢ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ ለእለ ፡ ይትዔወርዎ ፡ ወይገብሩ ፡ ከመዝ ፡ ወያቀውም ፡ ገጾ ፡ ላዕሌሆሙ ፡ እስከ ፡ ይሤርዎሙ ፡ እምድር ፡ ሕይወቶሙ ፡ ወያጠፍእ ፡ ዝክሮሙ ፡ እስከ ፡ ለዓለም ፤
sentences.l: Who kills soul-of blood innocent in-injustice and-in-secret cursed let-be; and-above-all not serve other gods, for jealous God toward those who-disregard(?)-him and-do thus, and-sets face-his against-them until he-uproots-them from-earth life-their and-blots-out memory-their until forever;
sentences.i: Whoever kills an innocent person wrongfully and in secret, let him be cursed. And above all, do not serve other gods, for God is jealous toward those who disregard (?) him and do so; he sets his face against them until he uproots their life from the earth and blots out their memory forever.
sentences.n: Deuteronomy 27:24-25 for the first curse (‘in secret’ is the በጒሕሉት of the curse above). ዘይቀትል ነፍሰ ደመ ንጹሐ: ነፍሰ ‘a person/soul’ then ደመ ንጹሐ ‘of innocent blood’, as I read it (?). Then the commandment of Exodus 20:3-5 and Deuteronomy 6:14-15: ወእምኵሉሰ ‘above all’ (እም + ኵሉ + -ሰ), ኢታምልኩ ‘do not serve’ (the same አምለከ as in ከመ ታምልክዎ above), ባዕደ አማልክተ ‘other gods’; ቀናኢ ‘jealous’. ለእለ ይትዔወርዎ ‘toward those who disregard him’ (ተዐወረ again, ‘turn a blind eye to’, here with God as object) (?). ያቀውም ገጾ ላዕሌሆሙ ‘sets his face against them’ is Leviticus 17:10 and 20:3; ይሤርዎሙ is ሠረወ ‘uproot’ + -ሙ with ሕይወቶሙ ‘their life’ in apposition; ወያጠፍእ ዝክሮሙ ‘and blots out their memory’ (cf. Deuteronomy 29:20, 9:14); እስከ ለዓለም ‘for ever’.

sentences.t: ብፁዓን ፡ እለ ፡ ይሰምዑ ፡ ቃለ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ ወይገብሩ ፡ ወየዐቅቡ ፡ ወብፁዓን ፡ እለ ፡ ይትገሐሡ ፡ እምእለ ፡ ይገብሩ ፡ እኩየ ፡ ከመ ፡ ኢትርክቦሙ ፡ እምእንተ ፡ ትመጽእ ፡ መቅሠፍት ፡ ለኃጥኣን ፤
sentences.l: Blessed-ones those who-hear word-of God and-do and-keep; and-blessed-ones those who-turn-aside from-those who-do evil, so-that not-reach-them from-what comes scourge to-sinners;
sentences.i: Blessed are those who hear the word of God and do it and keep it; and blessed are those who turn aside from those who do evil, so that nothing reaches them of the scourge that comes upon sinners;
sentences.n: ብፁዓን ‘blessed ones’ (the plural of ብፁዕ; no copula, as in the Beatitudes; cf. Luke 11:28 (hearing and keeping the word of God)). እለ ይሰምዑ ‘those who hear’ (እለ is the plural relative); the verbs are ይገብሩ ‘they do’, የዐቅቡ ‘they keep’, ይትገሐሡ ‘they turn aside’ (see ተገሐሡ above). እምእለ ይገብሩ እኩየ ‘from those who do evil’. ከመ ኢትርክቦሙ ‘so that it not reach them’; መቅሠፍት ለኃጥኣን ‘scourge to the sinners’ recalls Psalm 31:10 (LXX; ‘many are the scourges of the sinner’).

sentences.t: ወለእመሰ ፡ ኮንከ ፡ ዘተዐቅብ ፡ ቃለ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ ተገሐሥ ፡ እምፍኖተ ፡ ኃጥኣን ፡ ከመ ፡ ኢትዘበጥ ፡ በእንተ ፡ ተዘብጡ ፡ በበትር ፤
sentences.l: And-if-indeed you-be who-keeps word-of God, turn-aside from-way-of sinners, lest you-be-struck because they-were-struck with-rod;
sentences.i: And if you are one who keeps the word of God, turn aside from the way of sinners, lest you be struck because they were struck with the rod;
sentences.n: ወለእመሰ ‘and if indeed’; ኮንከ ‘you were/are’ (2ms perfect of ኮነ) with ዘተዐቅብ ‘who keeps’ (2ms imperfect). ተገሐሥ is the singular imperative (cf. ተገሐሡ above). ከመ ኢትዘበጥ ‘lest you be struck’ (the passive ተዘብጠ, from ዘይዘብጥ above). በእንተ ተዘብጡ ‘because they were struck’ (በእንተ ‘because of’ + a perfect); በበትር ‘with the rod’. The ‘rod’ prepares the Psalm quotation of the next unit.

sentences.t: በከመ ፡ ይቤ ፡ ዳዊት ፡ አበ ፡ አቡሁ ፡ ለእግዚእነ ፡ ዳዊት ፡ እስመ ፡ ኢየኀድግ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ በትረ ፡ ኃጥኣን ፡ ዲበ ፡ መክፈልተ ፡ ጻድቃን ፡ ከመ ፡ ኢያንሥኡ ፡ እደዊሆሙ ፡ ጻድቃን ፡ በዐመፃ ፤
sentences.l: As said David father-of father-his of-our-lord David: for not leaves God rod-of sinners upon portion-of righteous, so-that not raise hands-their righteous in-injustice;
sentences.i: As David said, the father of the father of our lord David: “For God will not leave the rod of sinners upon the lot of the righteous, so that the righteous do not lift their hands to injustice.”
sentences.n: A quotation of Psalm 125:3 (LXX 124:3), the ‘rod of the wicked’ over the ‘lot of the righteous’ (መክፈልት ‘portion, lot’ in the construct state, ‘lot of the righteous’; በትረ ኃጥኣን ‘rod of sinners’; ኢየኀድግ ‘does not leave’; ከመ ኢያንሥኡ ‘that they not lift up’; እደዊሆሙ ‘their hands’; በዐመፃ ‘to/in injustice’). ዳዊት አበ አቡሁ ለእግዚእነ ዳዊት is ‘David, father of the father of our lord David’: the king the party calls ‘our lord’ is Menelik, styled David since ch. 87, and King David is his father’s father; so this is not Christ (?). The name ዳዊት stands twice and I keep both.

sentences.t: ለእመ ፡ ተክህ ፡ ሎ ፡ ለብእሲ ፡ ይግበር ፡ ሠናየ ፡ ለሊሁኒ ፡ ይዕቀብ ፡ ወለቢጹኒ ፡ ይንግር ፡ ከመ ፡ ይኩን ፡ ባዕለ ፡ ክልኤ ፡ መካልይ ፡ ወይትወሰኮ ፡ ክልኤ ፡ መካልይ ፡ ወይከውን ፡ ትርብዕተ ፡ ዐስቡ ፡ በኀበ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ እስመ ፡ ገብረ ፡ ለሊሁ ፡ ወመህረ ፡ ለቢጹ ፡ ወበእንተዝ ፡ ይፈደፍድ ፡ ዐስቡ ፤
sentences.l: If was-possible to-him for-man to-do good, himself-too let-him-keep and-to-neighbour-his-too let-him-tell, that he-be owner-of two measures(?) and-be-added-to-him two measures and-be fourfold(?) reward-his with God, for did himself and-taught to-neighbour-his, and-for-this increases reward-his;
sentences.i: If a man is able to do good, let him keep it himself, and let him tell his neighbour also, so that he may be the owner of two measures (?), and two more measures be added to him, and his reward with God be fourfold (?); for he did it himself and taught his neighbour, and for this his reward grows;
sentences.n: A saying in the manner of the Gospel parables (Luke 19:8 for ‘fourfold’ (?); ‘he did and taught’ resembles Matthew 5:19 (?)), not a direct quotation. ተክህ ሎ ‘it was possible for him’ (ተክህለ ‘be able’, impersonal) ለብእሲ ‘for a man’; ለሊሁኒ ‘he himself too’ (ለሊሁ + -ኒ), ለቢጹኒ ‘and to his neighbour too’. ባዕለ ክልኤ መካልይ ‘owner of two measures’ (the construct state again; ‘measures’ for መካልይ is my guess (?)); ይትወሰኮ is the passive of ወሰከ ‘add’ + -ኦ ‘to him’. ትርብዕተ ‘fourfold’ (?), ዐስቡ ‘his reward’ (ዐስብ + -ሁ). The causes (እስመ ገብረ ለሊሁ ወመህረ ለቢጹ, ‘he did and taught’) are the reasons; ወበእንተዝ ‘and for this’ (በእንተ + ዝ); ይፈደፍድ is the quadriradical ‘increase, be multiplied’.

sentences.t: ወካዕበ ፡ ብፁዓን ፡ ትከውኑ ፡ ለእመ ፡ ወሀብክሙ ፡ ንዋይክሙ ፡ ዘእንበለ ፡ ርዴ ፡ ወልቃሕ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨
sentences.l: And-again blessed-ones you-be if you-give goods-your without interest(?) and-ልቃሕ(?) ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨
sentences.i: And again, you will be blessed if you give your goods without interest or demand for repayment (?). ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨
sentences.n: The closing precept is the law against usury (Exodus 22:25, Leviticus 25:36-37, Deuteronomy 23:19-20, Psalm 15:5). ወካዕበ ‘and again’; ብፁዓን ትከውኑ ‘you will be blessed’ (the plural predicate with ትከውኑ ‘you will be’). ወሀብክሙ is the 2mp perfect ‘you give’ (with ለእመ ‘if’). ዘእንበለ ርዴ ወልቃሕ ‘without ርዴ and ልቃሕ’: I take ርዴ as ‘interest, increase’ and ልቃሕ as ‘taking back, loan-claim’ (?), uncertain without Dillmann. The five ፨ at the end close the chapter and belong to this last unit.
